A transcriptional response would require membrane damage severe enough to trigger stress signaling within 6-24 h at 10 micromolar.
Detergent-like membrane disruption typically causes necrosis rather than a robust, reproducible transcriptional program in adherent cell lines.
falsifiers: Reproducible induction of unfolded protein response genes (e.g., HSPA5, XBP1, DDIT3, HERPUD1) at 6 h across multiple lines.
Reproducible induction of oxidative stress or heat shock genes (e.g., HMOX1, HSPA1A, DNAJB1) at 6 h.
Consistent activation of apoptosis or DNA damage response programs at 24 h.
A shared, dose-dependent transcriptional signature across the nine cell lines.
